name: Sri Veera Venkata Satyanarayana Swamy Vari Devasthanam
address: Executive Officer, Sri Veera Venkata Satyanarayana Swamy Vari Devasthanam, Annavaram - 533406, East Godavari District, Andhra Pradesh
main_deity: Lord Sri Veera Venkata Satyanarayana Swamy (Hari Hara Hiranya Garbha Thrimurtyatmaka)
description: Annavaram is one of the most famous Holy Shrines in India and enjoys second place after Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh. The temple is built in the Dravidian style. The glory and richness of Lord Satyadeva was widely described in Revakhanda of Skandapuranam. The presiding deity Lord Satyadeva with his consort Sri Anantha Lakshmi on one side and with Lord Siva on the other side took his abode on Ratnagiri, which is named after Ratnakara, son of Meru the king of holy mountains. Like in all Divyakshetrams surrounded and followed by holy rivers, Sri Satyanarayana Swamy at Annavaram is also followed by the sacred Pampa River touching the feet of the hill. Lord Satyadeva, the god of truth, showers his eternal blessings on mankind in his beautiful manifested form of the DIVINE TRINITY namely Hari Hara Hiranya Garbha Thrimurtyatmaka. Hence this temple attracts pilgrims of both Vaishnava and Saiva devotees, and thousands of pilgrims from all over the country worship Lord Satyadeva every day forgetting all sectional differences. The temple is enriched by the installation of SRIMATHRIPATHVIBHUTI VYKHUNTA MAHA NARAYANA YANTRA, which plays a dominant and important role with the power of attraction of both money and men (Dhana Janakarsha). The Peetham of Swamyvaru is highly adorned with the installation of Panchayatana, befitting the glory and sanctity of the deity. This famous yantra is a unique one, the like of which does not exist anywhere else in India.
history: It is believed that the place was known for constant food distribution (free feeding) by the benevolent people of the locality and that therefore the place was called by the name Annavaram ('annam' means food in Telugu). Another version is that because the presiding deity of the place blesses the devotees with aninavaram (pronounced or wanted boon), the place is called Annavaram. Ratnagiri Hill ranges are said to be connected with two strategic incidents: tradition says that Sri Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagar used the secret underground passages in the hills to attack the enemy from both sides during his invasion on Kalinga kings; and the Andhra revolutionary late Alluri Seetharama Raju had some of the secret quarters for himself and his followers in these hill ranges when he rebelled against the British Rule. It is said that one Brahmin of the village by name Earanki Prakasam got a dream wherein the Lord appeared and told him that his vigraha was left abandoned on the hill without worship and they shall trace it and reconsecrate it. That Brahmin informed Sri Raja I. V. Ramarayanam, the then Zamindar of Gorasa of Kirlampudi estate, and both of them along with other villagers traced the idol on the hill, worshipped it, and installed it at the present spot on Sravana Suddha Vidiya of the Telugu year Khara (1891 A.D. / Fasli 1301). The main temple was constructed on the hill with the pleasing and distant view of Bay of Bengal (11 miles) on one side and the row of Eastern Ghats on the other side, green fields around the hills, and the Pampa River encircling Ratnagiri. The hillock itself is about 300 feet above sea level, and about 300 well-laid stone steps lead to the top of it. Initially a small shed was constructed in 1891 when the idol was found. Later a temple was built in course of time with the cooperation of villagers and other devotees. Subsequently the temple was reconstructed during 1933-34 with locally available stone, and when it reached a dilapidated condition, it was reconstructed during 2011-2012.
mythology: The hillock by the side of the village is considered to be very sacred. Meruvu, the lord of the hills, and his consort Menaka did great penance and begot two sons by the grace of Lord Vishnu. One was named Bhadra and the other Ratnakar. Bhadra pleased Lord Vishnu with his devotion and penance and with his grace became Bhadrachalam on which Lord Sri Rama had permanently settled. Ratnakara desired to emulate his brother and succeeded in pleasing Lord Vishnu by his penance to settle on him as Veera Venkata Satyanarayanaswamy, Ratnakara remaining as Ratnagiri (hill).

sub_temples.name: Sri Rama Temple (Ramalayam)
sub_temples.significance: The adjoining shrine of Sri Rama is the holy spot where the original self-manifested idol of Sri Satyanarayanaswamy was discovered by the devotees. Lord Sri Rama is considered to be the Kshetra Palaka of this holy abode of Lord Satyadeva.

sub_temples.name: Sri Vana Durga Shrine
sub_temples.significance: Held in great veneration; Devi is said to be seen even to this day in the nights, going about the holy precincts perpetually guarding the Lord's premises.

sub_temples.name: Sri Kanaka Durga Shrine
sub_temples.location: Near the main temple precincts on Ratnagiri hill
sub_temples.significance: Dedicated shrine of Goddess Kanaka Durga where special poojas and Jatara Mahotsavams are performed.

sub_temples.name: Gramadevatha Nerellamma Temple
sub_temples.location: In the village at the foot of the hill
sub_temples.significance: Temple of the local village deity (Gramadevatha) protecting the foothills and the settlement.

sub_temples.name: Yantralayam (Panchayatana Shrine)
sub_temples.location: Ground floor of the main temple
sub_temples.significance: Contains the unique Srimathripathvibhuthi Vykhunta Maha Narayana Yantra and the Peetham of the Lord, with four deities on the four sides: Ganapati, Suryanarayanaswamy, Bala Tripurasundari, and Maheswaraswamy.

architecture.style: Dravidian style with unique chariot-shaped multi-tiered structure representing Agni Purana and Silpa Sastra cosmological principles.

highlights.name: Chariot Shaped Vimana & Temple Architecture
highlights.description: The main temple is constructed in the form of a chariot with four wheels at each of the four corners. The Akriti depicts the idea from Agni Purana and Silpa Sastra that the wall and vimana remind a devotee of the universe, with the chariot symbolizing the seven lokas underneath and seven lokas above, and the Garbhalaya at the heart center ruling over the entire universe. The wheels depicting the Sun and the Moon serve to remind that this Jaggernaut moves on the wheels of time forever.

highlights.name: Unique 13-Feet Cylindrical Trimurti Idol
highlights.description: The idol is about 13 feet high in a cylindrical form across two floors. The base is in the lower sanctum representing Lord Brahma (creator), the middle portion represents Lord Siva (destroyer), and the top is in the upper sanctum representing Lord Vishnu (protector). All three of the Divine Trinity are clubbed and worshipped simultaneously in a single idol encaged in gold kavachams.

highlights.name: Two-Tier Sanctum Layout (Ground & First Floor)
highlights.description: The temple is built on two floors. The ground floor houses the sacred Srimathripathvibhuthi Vykhunta Maha Narayana Yantra, the Peetham, and the Panchayatana deities (Ganapati, Suryanarayanaswamy, Bala Tripurasundari, Maheswaraswamy). The first floor contains the Moola Virat of Lord Satyanarayanaswamy in the centre, Goddess Sri Anantha Lakshmi Ammavaru on the right, and Lord Shiva on the left.

highlights.name: Kalyana Mantapa & Stone Steps
highlights.description: In front of the main temple is the Kalyana Mantapa constructed and decorated with modern pieces of architecture. About 300 well-laid stone steps lead from the foothills up 300 feet above sea level to the temple top, offering views of the Eastern Ghats, lush green fields, Pampa River, and the distant Bay of Bengal (11 miles).
